summary: This article explains how gardens on roofs cool buildings and cities, grow food, shelter wildlife, and soak up rain, and what builders must plan to make them work.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “Rooftop Gardens”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: a hard building material made of cement, sand, stones, and water
to change from a liquid into a gas
the natural home of an animal or plant

challengeTerms.def: having to do with a city
material that slows heat from moving in or out
the variety of different living things in a place

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that every school should have a garden on its roof? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two ways a rooftop garden helps cool a city, and describe one challenge of building one.
struggling: Pre-teach concrete, evaporate, and habitat with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use urban, insulation, and biodiversity in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
